subject: HighWater POC — traffic metrics, evaluation plan, and owners
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@highwater.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: HighWater POC — traffic metrics, evaluation plan, and owners

Alex — thanks for the call today. Good alignment on scope and value props; below is a concise recap and actions so we can get the trial standing up next week. Please reply inline where anything needs correction.

Summary of what we heard from HighWater (confirm):
- Primary workload: real-time semantic search for customer support (chat -> vector search -> rerank).
- Request profile: 600 sustained RPS expected during business hours, with 2–3 daily bursts up to ~1,800 RPS for short windows (2–5 minutes).
- Typical payloads: user messages average ~45 tokens; system prompts add ~30 tokens; average response target ~80 tokens.
- Concurrency: ~220 concurrent chat sessions during peak sustained windows.
- Latency expectation: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for the tiered search path (embedding + rerank).

Proposed success criteria (initial):
1) Functional parity: LLM responses equal or better than their internal baseline on sample prompt set (we'll run A/B on identical prompts).
2) Performance: 95th p99 generation + rerank < 350ms at target sustained load (600 RPS) and graceful degradation during bursts (timeouts/retry metrics).
3) Cost: token cost per 1k requests within agreed range (we'll provide estimates once we confirm batching and quantization settings).
4) Operational: stable KV cache hit rate >= 60% for prefix-heavy queries during the run.

Immediate asks (for intake):
- Can you share a 24–72 hour traffic sample in JSONL format (timestamps, request id, session id, prompt token count, response token count, path taken)? Attachment stub is fine — we discussed one on the call.
- Confirm peak burst duration and frequency (are bursts usually 2–5 minutes, daily?)
- Any rate limits or network egress constraints on your side (VPC/proxy) we should know about?
- Which evaluation prompts are highest priority? We need a short list (10–20) for the initial quality readout.

Proposed timeline (we can tighten):
- Apr 5: Receive traffic sample + success-criteria doc from HighWater.
- Apr 6–7: Redwood sets up dedicated trial environment and ingests sample; initial perf smoke test.
- Apr 9: Demo + quality readout (A/B) with your team.
- Apr 12: Trial stabilization and cost tuning; follow-up on contract terms.

Owners / next steps:
- Marcus (me): overall trial owner, environment provisioning, and lead demo.
- Aditya Rao: workload mapping and perf tuning (batching, KV cache config).
- Marissa Cole: evals and quality metrics (prompt sets, A/B comparisons).

Attachments: I attached a sample success criteria template (poc_success_criteria.docx). Also please upload the traffic sample to the Drive link and reply here.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
[Attachment: poc_success_criteria.docx]

Subject: Re: HighWater POC — traffic metrics, evaluation plan, and owners

Thanks Alex — received the sample and the priority prompt list. Quick follow-ups after a first pass through the sample:

Questions we found while scanning the export:
- There are short sustained windows where avg token lengths jump to ~420 tokens (likely long transcripts). Can you mark whether those are full-conversation dumps vs single-turn submissions?
- A small subset of requests include binary attachments (images). Are those routed to the LLM pipeline or handled separately? If routed, we'll need expected tokenization behavior.

Technical plan for trial environment (high level):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated trial pool (3 x A100 equiv) with autoscale to 5 nodes for bursts; we will instrument KV caching on the prefix-heavy flows.
- Engine settings: 8-bit quantization profile for rerank model; continuous batching with 20–30ms latency cap; prefix cache TTL initially set to 10 minutes.
- Observability: we'll surface token-level cost, per-route p95/p99, and KV cache hit rate to the Drive dashboard.

Request: please confirm the two items above and share any locations in the sample marked as retention-sensitive so we can redact before wider distribution to the infra team.

I'll start provisioning; Aditya will take point on workload mapping tomorrow.

—
Marcus

On it — I ran a quick mapping against our throughput model and a few notes / preliminary numbers: 

- Sustained 600 RPS scenario: with 8-bit quantization + continuous batching (20ms cap) we expect p95 gen latency ~220–280ms on the proposed 3-node pool; cost estimate ~0.28 USD / 1k requests (est).
- Burst behavior (1,900 RPS for 3–6 minutes): we can absorb with autoscale to 5 nodes but p99 will spike; recommend a soft-failover to a cheaper fallback model for rerank path during burst windows to keep p95 <500ms.
- Long-token windows (~420 tokens): these increase compute per request by ~3–4x; if these are full transcript uploads we should route them to an async pipeline or cap response length for the trial.

ETA: I will post a detailed workload mapping doc to the Drive and share batch/quantization config by EOD today. Marissa — I flagged the 5 blocker prompts in the Drive under /evaluation/blockers.

Aditya
